title: Design and implement hybrid partitioning + cost-tiering for audit log ingestion and retention
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Problem: Our current audit ingestion creates daily high-cardinality indices that drive up cluster storage and query cost for long-tail customers. We also lack a consistent mechanism for per-organization retention SLAs, compacting low-value telemetry, and surfacing RBAC/SSO metadata required for compliance queries.

Goal: Implement a hybrid hot/warm/cold partitioning model plus cost-tiering and compaction for audit logs. This ticket covers ingestion tagging, partition key design, index lifecycle policies (ILM), compaction/rollup jobs, and admin controls to let tenants and operators configure retention tiers. The solution must preserve full-fidelity for high-priority events (privileged actions, admin changes, auth failures) while aggressively compressing or rolling-up low-value events to control unit economics.

Constraints:
- Must integrate with RBAC v2 changes (actor_id, role_changes) and SSO/SAML session metadata so audits remain queryable by compliance teams.
- Maintain ability to export full raw events for eDiscovery within configured retention windows.
- Work must not regress existing SLOs for ingest latency (<200ms p95) or query latency for hot indices.
- Prefer reuse of existing components (kafka ingestion topics, existing search cluster) where safe; introduce new components only when cost justified.
acceptance_criteria: Ingestion pipeline tags events with tenant_id_hash, event_priority, and sso_session_id for every audit event.
Hot/Warm/Cold ILM policies deployed: hot (0-7d), warm (8-90d), cold (91d+) with automated rollover and shrink/merge steps.
Compaction jobs produce daily rollup documents for low-priority event types (counts + top-n metadata) and delete compacted raw events after configurable window.
Per-tenant retention SLA can be set from Console and enforced by storage policies (default: 90d; enterprise-customizable up to 7 years).
Query routing sends searches for >90d data to cold store and supports on-demand rehydration for full-text returns.
Storage cost comparison report showing >=30% reduction in monthly storage cost for long-tail tenants in pilot (after compaction + cold tiering).
Automated e2e test covering tag propagation, ILM transitions, compaction success, and export functionality.
Security review completed; SSO/SAML session linkage verified in audit events; KMS used for cold storage encryption.
implementation_plan: 1) Add tenant_id_hash, event_priority, sso_session_id, and actor_role fields to the ingest schema and forwarder (edge producer changes).
2) Create new kafka topic 'audit-compaction-commands' for compaction orchestration; keep raw ingestion topic unchanged for compatibility.
3) Update ingestion service to set partition_key = sha256(tenant_id) % N_shards + "-YYYY.MM.DD" and route to hot index stream.
4) Implement ILM templates: daily rollover in hot, force merge/shrink in warm, snapshot/transfer to S3 cold tier in cold. Use index aliases for transparent queries.

5) Build compaction worker that reads raw events for a tenant/day, produces aggregated rollups (counts, top actors, anomalous patterns) and writes to compacted index; mark raw docs eligible for deletion after retain_window.
6) Console controls: per-tenant retention UI, cost estimation, and one-click request to export raw data for eDiscovery (trigger rehydration job).
7) Add audit-metadata enrichment step for RBAC v2: resolve actor_id -> current_role snapshot and include role_change events as high-priority; ensure SAML session id persists through retries.
8) Deploy ILM and compaction to staging, run full load test with synthetic tenant mix, measure ingest/query latency and storage footprint, iterate.
migration_plan: Phase A (pilot): Select 5 long-tail tenants and enable compaction + cold tiering. Monitor for 2 weeks and collect cost/latency metrics.
Phase B (gradual rollout): Auto-enroll tenants with <X qps and >Y retention into hybrid tiering; allow opt-out via Console for dev/test orgs.
Phase C (full): Backfill compaction for last 12 months for tenants who opt-in for archive compression; provide export option for full raw rehydrate.
testing_plan: Unit tests for schema changes and enrichment logic.
Integration tests for ILM transitions (hot->warm->cold) in staging cluster using simulated traffic.
Load tests to verify ingest p95 <200ms and compaction jobs do not starve hot path.
Compliance tests verifying that privileged events retain full fidelity for 7 years when tenant SLA requires.
monitoring_and_alerting: New Grafana dashboard: 'Audit Storage - Hot/Warm/Cold' with index size, doc counts, ILM state, compaction failure rate.
Cost budget alert: projected monthly storage for tenant > 150% of baseline (ops-notify + tenant-warning).
decisions: Use hybrid hot/warm/cold with S3 cold snapshots instead of long-term monthly indices to reduce cluster shard count.
Compaction will be tenant-scoped; default compaction window is 24h and configurable per tenant via Console.
Keep raw events for high-priority types (auth_fail, role_change, admin_action) until configured enterprise retention; other types eligible for rollup after 7d.
